title: the flute
tomorrow: the rasa lila (with the Keeper's framing)

segments.voice: Yesterday: the flute again, and a gopi jealous of a piece of bamboo, until she saw the rivers and trees that raised it and grew glad.
screen: `THE FLUTE.` · `JEALOUS OF A REED, THEN GLAD.`

segments.voice: The milk is on the fire. Someone is halfway through milking a cow. Someone is serving food to her family. Someone has a baby at her breast. It's an autumn night in Vraja, the moon full and coming up red over the trees, and every house is in the middle of something. Then, from the forest, the flute. Not the daytime music the gopis talked about from a distance. This time, the Bhagavata says, the sound is calling them.
screen: `THE MILK IS ON THE FIRE.` → `A FULL MOON OVER THE TREES.` → `THIS TIME, THE FLUTE CALLS.`

segments.voice: The text slows down and goes house by house. The women hear the flute and go, each one exactly as she is. The one milking leaves the cow. The one boiling milk leaves the pot on the fire. The one cooking leaves the food unserved. The one feeding a child, the one waiting on her husband, the one eating her own dinner: all of them stand up and go. Some were dressing or putting on makeup, and they go with their clothes and ornaments in disarray. Husbands, fathers and brothers try to stop them; they don't turn around. And some, the Bhagavata adds, were kept inside, and those women shut their eyes and went to him in meditation instead. Why linger on the half-finished jobs? Because the list is the point. Nobody finishes anything, waits for a better time, or makes herself presentable first. Devotional readers hear a picture of the soul when God calls: it doesn't arrive polished, it arrives as it is, mid-task, with the milk still on the stove. And the Bhagavata doesn't let the scene pass unexamined. Right after this, the king who's listening stops the story to ask how a love like theirs could set anyone free, and Krishna himself will tell the women to go home. That's where tomorrow begins. Tonight, the scene is enough: a village full of unfinished things, and women on the road into the trees, running toward a sound.
screen: `EACH ONE GOES EXACTLY AS SHE IS.` · `SOME KEPT INSIDE GO IN MEDITATION.` · `NOBODY FINISHES ANYTHING FIRST.` · then, large: `MID-TASK, AS SHE IS.`

segments.voice: Notice what you just set down to be here, a phone, a cup, a list, and leave it untidied. Let your attention arrive as you are, unfinished, and when the half-done things tug, notice the tug and stay. If you pray, come to God, or to Krishna, just as you are, without fixing anything first.
The flute. On the autumn night, the sound that calls the gopis out of their houses, mid-task, just as they are.
Your line: mid-task, as she is. Nobody in that list arrived ready. That's day eight hundred ninety-nine.

chat.says: In that Krishna story, why don't the women finish their chores before going?
options: Because the list is the point: when the call comes, each goes as she is, mid-task.
Because Krishna ordered them to hurry, and they were afraid of being punished.
Because their husbands sent them out to bring the cows home before dark.
chat.meaning: The Bhagavata lists the half-done jobs on purpose: nobody finishes or tidies up first. Readers hear the soul answering God's call as it is.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.29, the autumn night: the flute calls and the gopis leave their tasks

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm the list of interrupted tasks against Bhagavata 10.29 (roughly verses 4–8): milking, milk on the fire, cooking/serving, feeding children, serving husbands, eating, dressing and makeup; relatives trying to stop them; some kept inside who meditated on him.
The text says the women kept inside attained him in meditation (some readings: left their bodies); the script keeps only 'went to him in meditation'. A Keeper should decide how much to say.
'The moon coming up red' is in the scene-setting of 10.29.2 as I recall it; confirm or cut.
The line that the story 'isn't asking anyone to walk out on their family' anticipates the Keeper's framing for day 900; a Keeper may want to shape this.
The devotional reading (the soul arriving as it is) is attributed to 'devotional readers'; confirm.
Editor pass: review question now checks day 898's carry (turning envy into gladness) rather than the practice.
